nv.name: Melanocytic Nevus
nv.explanation: A common type of benign skin lesion composed of melanocytes (pigment cells). These are typically harmless moles or birthmarks.
general_precautions: Monitor existing moles for changes in size, shape, or color
Protect from excessive sun exposure with sunscreen (SPF 30+)
Wear protective clothing and seek shade when outdoors
Avoid tanning beds and artificial UV exposure
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Avoid scratching or irritating the mole
Use gentle, fragrance-free skincare products
Moisturize regularly to maintain skin health
avoid: Picking, scratching, or attempting to remove the mole yourself
Excessive sun exposure without protection
Using harsh chemicals or irritants on the area
Self-examination tools that could damage the skin
warning_signs: Change in color (especially darkening or multiple colors)
New symptoms such as pain or tenderness
nv.urgency_text: Routine monitoring is sufficient. If any warning signs appear, schedule a dermatologist appointment within 2-4 weeks.

mel.name: Melanoma
mel.explanation: A serious form of skin cancer that develops from pigment-producing cells (melanocytes). It can spread to other parts of the body if not detected early.
general_precautions: Perform regular skin self-examinations monthly
Protect from sun exposure with broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 30+
Avoid tanning beds completely
Wear sun-protective clothing when outdoors
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Do not apply harsh chemicals or irritants
Use gentle, fragrance-free products
Protect from further sun exposure until evaluated
avoid: Delaying medical evaluation
Attempting self-diagnosis or home remedies
Ignoring changes in the lesion
Using over-the-counter treatments without medical advice
warning_signs: ABCDE signs: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter >6mm, Evolving changes
mel.urgency_text: Seek immediate medical evaluation. Melanoma requires prompt diagnosis and treatment. Schedule a dermatologist appointment within 48 hours or visit urgent care if rapidly changing.

bcc.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
bcc.explanation: The most common type of skin cancer, typically appearing as a pearly bump or pinkish growth. It rarely spreads but can cause local tissue damage if untreated.
general_precautions: Protect from sun exposure with sunscreen SPF 30+
Wear protective clothing and seek shade
Avoid tanning beds
Regular skin examinations, especially if you have fair skin
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Avoid scratching or irritating the lesion
Use gentle skincare products
Do not apply cosmetics or makeup to the area until evaluated
avoid: Attempting to remove or treat the lesion yourself
Ignoring persistent sores that don't heal
Applying home remedies or alternative medicines
Delaying medical evaluation
warning_signs: Visible blood vessels within the lesion
Slow growth over months or years
bcc.urgency_text: Schedule a dermatologist appointment within 1-2 weeks. While not immediately life-threatening, basal cell carcinoma should be evaluated and treated to prevent tissue damage.

akiec.name: Actinic Keratosis
akiec.explanation: A rough, scaly patch caused by years of sun exposure. It is considered a precancerous lesion that may develop into squamous cell carcinoma if left untreated.
general_precautions: Strict sun protection with sunscreen SPF 30+
Wear wide-brimmed hats and protective clothing
Avoid peak sun hours (10 AM - 4 PM)
Use lip balm with SPF protection
skin_care: Keep the area moisturized
Use gentle exfoliation only if recommended by dermatologist
Apply moisturizing creams to reduce roughness
Avoid harsh scrubs or peels
avoid: Picking or scratching off scales
Using harsh chemical peels without medical supervision
Continuing unprotected sun exposure
Self-treatment with over-the-counter wart removers
warning_signs: Development of a lump or nodule
akiec.urgency_text: Schedule a dermatologist appointment within 1-2 weeks. Actinic keratosis can be treated easily in early stages but may progress to cancer if left untreated.

bkl.name: Benign Keratosis-like Lesions
bkl.explanation: Includes seborrheic keratoses, solar lentigines, and other benign growths. These are non-cancerous but should be monitored for changes.
general_precautions: Sun protection with sunscreen SPF 30+
Regular skin examinations
Avoid picking or scratching lesions
Monitor for any changes in appearance
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Use gentle moisturizers
Avoid harsh chemicals or irritants
Do not attempt to remove the lesion yourself
avoid: Picking, scratching, or trying to scrape off the lesion
Using over-the-counter wart or mole removers
Applying acids or harsh chemicals
Self-removal tools or home remedies
warning_signs: Rapid growth or increase in size
New symptoms such as pain or itching
bkl.urgency_text: Routine monitoring is generally sufficient. However, if the lesion changes or causes concern, schedule a dermatologist appointment within 2-4 weeks for evaluation.

df.name: Dermatofibroma
df.explanation: A benign firm nodule that often appears on the legs. It consists of fibrous tissue and is typically harmless, but can be mistaken for other skin conditions.
general_precautions: Monitor for any changes in size or appearance
Protect from trauma or injury to the area
Maintain regular skin examinations
Document the lesion with photos for comparison
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Use gentle skincare products
Avoid applying harsh chemicals or irritants
Do not attempt to manipulate or compress the lesion
avoid: Attempting to remove or excise the lesion yourself
Repeatedly touching or manipulating the area
Applying creams or treatments without medical advice
Ignoring rapid changes in the lesion
warning_signs: Development of new symptoms in surrounding skin
df.urgency_text: Routine monitoring is generally appropriate. If the lesion changes or causes concern, schedule a dermatologist appointment within 2-4 weeks for evaluation.

vasc.name: Vascular Lesions
vasc.explanation: Abnormal growths formed from blood vessels. These include cherry angiomas, spider angiomas, and other vascular malformations. Most are benign but should be evaluated.
general_precautions: Protect from trauma or injury to the area
Avoid scratching or picking at the lesion
Monitor for bleeding or rapid growth
Maintain regular skin examinations
skin_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Apply gentle pressure if bleeding occurs
Use soft, non-irritating bandages if needed
Avoid harsh chemicals or irritants
avoid: Picking, scratching, or traumatizing the lesion
Attempting to remove or cauterize the lesion yourself
Using scissors, razors, or home removal tools
Applying creams or treatments without medical advice
warning_signs: Ulceration or breakdown of the overlying skin
vasc.urgency_text: Schedule a dermatologist appointment within 1-2 weeks. While many vascular lesions are benign, persistent bleeding or changes should be evaluated to rule out other conditions.
